title: Stereotactic Orthotopic Xenograft Injections into the Mouse Brain
protocol: Typrsinize cultured cells in the tissue culture room.
Wash cells with sterile PBS.
Resuspend cells in sterile PBS to an adjusted final volume of at least 100,000 cells per 3ul injection.
Transport resuspended cells to the injection area on ice.
Assemble the stereotaxic device according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Lay out the drill and drill bit.
Turn on the heating pad and monitor its temperature with a thermometer.
Prepare the Hamilton syringe by rinsing in 70% Ethanol.
Rinse the Hamilton syringe with sterile PBS.
Gently resuspend trypsinized cells in PBS.
Draw cells to 3uL in the Hamilton syringe, carefully avoiding bubbles.
Position the syringe in the stereotactic device.
Tighten the screw to lock the syringe in the correct position.
Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneal injection of Ketamine 100 mg/kg.
Confirm anesthetic effectiveness by toe pinch.
Wipe the mouse’s head 3 times with sterile cotton swab dipped in betadine.
Swab the area with an alcohol wipe.
Protect the mouse’s eyes by coating with sterile ocular lubricant.
Make a 1.5 cm sagittal incision in the mouse's scalp from the front to the back.
Position the mouse in the stereotactic apparatus.
Displace the tongue to the side with the wooden end of a sterile cotton swab.
Position the front teeth in the tooth holder.
Tighten the nose holder until firm.
Place both ears in the ear holders.
Tighten the ear holders until firm.
Wipe the skull with a sterile cotton swab to remove shiny membranes and aid identification of the bregma suture.
Drill a hole 2 mm right and 1 mm anterior to the bregma suture.
Lower the Hamilton syringe needle to the edge of the hole.
Lower the needle 3.5 mm into the brain.
Raise the needle 1 mm and wait 1 minute.
Inject 1 μL of cells, raise the needle 1 more mm, and wait 1 minute.
Inject 1 μL, raise 1 mm, and wait 1 minute.
Then inject the final 1 μL.
Completely remove the needle from the mouse’s brain.
Remove the mouse from the stereotaxic device.
Close the skin incision by holding the edges with forceps and applying one clip.
Place the mouse on the heating pad until the effects of anesthetic wear off.
Return the mouse to its cage when the anesthesia wears off.
Clean the Hamilton syringe with Hamilton cleaning solution.
Clean the Hamilton syringe with 70% ethanol.
Clean the Hamilton syringe with sterile water.
Administer analgesic twice a day for the first 3 days after surgery.
Remove sutures after 10 days.
Monitor mice daily for signs of neurologic compromise.
